_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 01:43:56Z)**_

I've implemented issue #48 on `feat/issue-48-motion-edit`. The typecheck is clean, `yarn fix` passes, and all 1572 tests pass, including 16 new ones in `packages/excalidraw/tests/pathEditing.test.tsx`. I haven't opened it in the browser with `yarn start`, so the toolbar's look and position and how the handles feel by hand are still unchecked. Nothing is committed.

**How it works:**

- **Entering edit mode:** right-click the path and choose **Edit motion path**, or double-click it. Right-clicking the element itself doesn't offer this option; clicking the element still edits it as a normal element.
- **In edit mode:**
  - **Points:** drag a point to move it, or drag a segment midpoint to add one.
  - **Removing points:** Delete removes the selected points, but a path always keeps at least 2.
  - **Whole path:** you can move, resize and rotate the path while editing its points.
- **Small toolbar:** buttons for **Test animation**, **Curved/Straight**, **Revert** and **Done**.
- **Revert vs confirm:** Delete with no points selected reverts the whole session (path and element). Clicking off, pressing Esc or clicking Done confirms it, and the element snaps onto the new start point.
- **No duplicates:** edits change the existing path in place; no new path or animation is created.
- **Playback:** the animation now uses the path as it appears on screen, so moved, resized, rotated and curved paths all play correctly.

**Behaviour changes from #45:**

- Paths now get resize and rotate handles even outside edit mode. #45 had turned them off, but selecting a path together with another element could already resize it and leave its points wrong; resizing now rescales the points properly.
- The test helper `API.createElement` now creates paths straight unless a test asks for a curve, matching how the path tool creates them. Before, it gave them round edges by default.

**Things I fixed along the way:**

- In edit mode, a path point often sits right on a resize handle, and the handle was grabbing the click. Points and midpoints now take priority over the handles.
- Finishing a resize or rotate of the path ended the edit session. It now stays open.

The curve is the same one Excalidraw's hit-testing uses for curved lines, so clicking the path and dragging its midpoints match what's drawn. Movement settings like speed are left out, as you chose.

The 133 snapshot updates are the new `motionPathEditor: null` state field, plus the new menu item appearing in the context-menu snapshot.

The edit-mode logic is in the new `actions/actionMotionPathEditor.tsx`, the toolbar in `components/MotionPathEditToolbar.tsx`, and the curve sampling in `element/src/pathSamples.ts`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 02:03:52Z)**_

Here's how to edit a motion path on the dev server after creating it.

**1. Start editing**

- **Right-click the dashed path line itself**, not the element it moves, and choose **Edit motion path**.
- Or **double-click the path line**. If it isn't selected yet, the first click of the double-click selects it.
- You'll know you're in edit mode when you see point handles on the path and a small toolbar to its top-right: **Test animation · Curved · Revert · Done**.

**2. Move points**

- Drag any point (the dots on the path) to a new spot.
- Drag the dashed line itself to move the whole path; the element moves with it.
- The corner handles resize the path, and the handle above it rotates it.

**3. Add points**

- Hover a segment and a small midpoint handle appears halfway between two points. Drag it to create a new point there.

**4. Delete points**

- Click a point to select it. Shift-click to select more than one.
- Press **Delete** or **Backspace**.
- A path always keeps at least 2 points, so deleting below that does nothing.

**5. Straight ↔ curved**

- Click **Curved** in the toolbar. The path becomes a smooth curve through every point.
- The button then reads **Straight**; click it to switch back.
- Points stay editable while curved.

**6. Preview**

- Click **Test animation**. The element plays along the edited path, then returns to its spot.

**7. Finish**

- **Keep your changes:** click empty canvas, press **Esc**, or click **Done**. The element snaps onto the path's new start point.
- **Throw away the whole session:** with no points selected, press **Delete**, or click **Revert**. The path and element go back to how they were when you entered edit mode.

These steps match what the automated tests cover; I haven't tried them in the browser myself. Two things are worth a close look on the dev server:

- **Hidden midpoint handles:** on very short segments they may not show, which is the same as for normal lines.
- **Points near a corner:** where a point sits close to a resize handle, clicking it should select the point rather than start a resize.

If anything behaves differently, tell me what you did and what happened and I'll fix it.

All three issues are fixed. The full suite passes (1576 tests), and lint and the typecheck are clean. I haven't tried these fixes on the dev server.

**1. The element now snaps back to the path after a resize or rotate.** Before, the element only snapped onto the path's start when the path was created and when you confirmed an edit session. Resizing or rotating the path, or resizing the element itself, left the two apart. Now, at the end of any resize or rotate that touches a path or its element, the element moves so it's centred on the path's start point again. This works in edit mode and with normal selection. Dragging points in edit mode still snaps only when you confirm, as before.

**2. Reject now actually restores the path.** The "before" copy of the path pointed at the live path instead of copying it. Since edits change the live path directly, every edit also changed the "before" copy, so rejecting just put back the edited version. That made it behave like Done. It now saves a real copy when you start editing. My earlier test had the same blind spot and only passed by accident. The new tests check against fixed values, and I confirmed they fail with the old code and pass with the fix.

**3. "Revert" is now "Reject".** I renamed it everywhere: the button label, the action, the code that Delete-with-nothing-selected uses, the test id, and the comments.

On the dev server, the end-to-end check is:

- **Reject:** open a path, move points, resize or rotate it, then click **Reject**. The path and element should go back exactly to how they were.
- **Snap:** outside edit mode, resize or rotate the path, or resize its element. The element should end up centred on the path's start.

Snapping happens only at the end of a mouse resize or rotate. Changing size or angle by typing into the Stats panel won't snap the element yet. I can add that if you use it.

Closes #48 (part of #18).

## Summary
A confirmed motion path can now be edited without recreating it. The element on the path is still edited as a normal element, and the path stays attached.

**Path editing:** right-click the path (or double-click it) and choose **Edit motion path**.
- Drag points to move them. Drag a segment midpoint to add a point. Select points and press Delete to remove them (a path always keeps at least 2).
- Move, resize or rotate the whole path with its handles.
- A small floating toolbar offers **Test animation**, **Curved/Straight**, **Reject** and **Done**.
- **Confirm:** clicking off, Esc or Done keeps the changes and snaps the element onto the path's new start.
- **Reject:** pressing Delete with no points selected, or clicking Reject, restores the path and element to how they were when editing started.

**Element editing:** clicking the element edits it as usual. Moving, resizing or rotating it keeps its path. After any resize or rotate of the path or its element, the element is re-snapped onto the path's start.

## Implementation notes
- `actions/actionMotionPathEditor.tsx` (new): adds the enter, finish, reject and curve-toggle actions. Edit state lives in `appState.motionPathEditor` with a copied snapshot of the path and element positions; it is not persisted.
- `components/MotionPathEditToolbar.tsx` (new): the floating toolbar.
- `element/src/pathSamples.ts` (new): samples the curved path. It uses the same Catmull-Rom curve as Excalidraw's curved-line hit-testing, so rendering, hit-testing, midpoint handles and playback all follow the same line.
- `path.ts` / `pathPlayback.ts`: alignment and playback now use the path's scene coordinates with rotation applied.
- **Re-enables resize and rotate for paths**, which #45 had disabled. `transformHandles.ts` and `resizeTest.ts` no longer block paths, and `resizeElements.ts` / `bounds.ts` rescale the points. Before this, multi-select resize could already reach paths and leave their points wrong.
- In edit mode, point and midpoint handles take priority over resize handles. Resizing or rotating the path doesn't end the edit session.
- The test helper `API.createElement` now creates paths straight by default, matching the path tool.

## Testing
- `yarn test:update`: 117 files and 1576 tests pass. Snapshot changes are the new `motionPathEditor: null` app-state field and the new context-menu entry.
- `yarn test:typecheck` and `yarn fix` are clean.
- New `tests/pathEditing.test.tsx` (20 cases) covers the menu entry, entering edit mode, moving, adding and deleting points, no duplicate paths, curve toggle, Test animation, Reject (verified to fail against the old snapshot bug), confirm-and-snap, Esc, resize and rotate of the path, and transforms keeping the element snapped and attached.
- Updated `element/tests/path.test.ts` with curve sampling, rotated alignment and point rescaling.
- Not checked in the browser yet. Typing size or angle into the Stats panel doesn't trigger the snap.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
